items.expected_literal:
Track open-close state of C-style /* ... */ comment blocks across the
whole source file. For each line, first advance the state machine over
the line contents while accumulating the non-comment substring of the
line. Then scan that non-comment substring for process_data(N): DESC
headers using a fixed regex and emit each match on its own line. The
state machine handles multiple opens and closes on a single line and
spans arbitrarily many lines between an open and its matching close.
This encoding CANNOT be expressed as a pure line-scoped ripgrep pattern
because /* ... */ comment blocks routinely span more than 200 lines,
so the agent MUST shell-pipeline through awk, sed with a state buffer,
or python to encode the state transitions.

items.expected_literal:
import re, sys
src = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
out = []
inc = False
i = 0
n = len(src)
buf = []
while i < n:
    if inc:
        j = src.find('*/', i)
        if j == -1:
            i = n
        else:
            inc = False
            i = j + 2
    else:
        j = src.find('/*', i)
        if j == -1:
            buf.append(src[i:])
            i = n
        else:
            buf.append(src[i:j])
            inc = True
            i = j + 2
outside = ''.join(buf)
for m in re.finditer(r'process_data\([0-9]+\): [A-Za-z0-9_ ]+', outside):
    print(m.group(0))

items.expected_literal:
Emit, on stdout, exactly one line per REAL process_data(N) traceback header
found in the source file, in the original source-file order (top to bottom).
A REAL header is one whose containing byte position is NOT inside a
C-style /* ... */ block comment. Shadow headers that occur inside an open
/* ... */ block are documentation, not real, and MUST NOT appear in the
output. Each emitted line MUST be exactly the substring
process_data(N): DESC where N is the numeric argument and DESC is the
description text that follows the colon-space, terminated by the first
double-quote, backslash, or newline. The output has exactly one LF per
emitted line, no trailing blank line.
